title: Stacked valuation configuration through a dense open of an algebraic space
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A valuation ring is as in [def-trf-valuation-ring]; an extension of valuation rings means an injective local ring homomorphism, where local means that the maximal ideal contracts to the maximal ideal. Let $p:H\to X$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces, and let $h:V\hookrightarrow H$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with dense image. Here quasi-compact means quasi-compact on affine scheme tests: the pullback to each affine scheme mapping to the target is a quasi-compact algebraic space. Let $A$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, and let $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$, $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to H$ satisfy $p\eta=a|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$. There exist a valuation ring $C$, a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset C$, an extension $A\hookrightarrow E=C/\mathfrak q$ of valuation rings, and morphisms $b:\operatorname{Spec}C\to X$, $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}D\to H$, $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to V$, where $D=C_{\mathfrak q}$ is localization at $C\setminus\mathfrak q$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}(C)=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$, with the following properties. The ring $D$ is a valuation ring, its residue field is $F=\operatorname{Frac}(E)$, and the inclusion $A\hookrightarrow E$ induces $K\hookrightarrow F$. Writing $j_D:\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}C$, $i_E:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}C$, and $s_F:\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ for the canonical maps, one has $$p\alpha=bj_D,\qquad \alpha|_{\operatorname{Spec}L}=hu,\qquad \alpha s_F=\eta\operatorname{Spec}(K\hookrightarrow F),\qquad bi_E=a\operatorname{Spec}(A\hookrightarrow E).$$ No separatedness, finite-type, quasi-compactness of $p$, or valuation lifting hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 089G (lemma-refined-valuative-criterion-universally-closed), proof from equation-start-with through the definition of C, before invoking assumption (4); affine-chart reduction uses Tag 089F, valuation probe Tag 089B, flat scheme-image base change Tag 089E, and stacking Tag 088Z (algebra-lemma-stack-valuation-rings).

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] with closed support $|H|$ to form $r:H_0=H_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow H$, and put $V_0=V\times_HH_0$. This is a quasi-compact open subspace of $H_0$, with the same dense point image as $V$; quasi-compactness follows directly on affine tests. Since $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is reduced, [lem-sfb-space-reduced-map-closed-factorization] factors $\eta$ through $H_0$. Set $p_0=pr$. The inclusion $j_0:V_0\hookrightarrow H_0$ is schematically dominant in the closed-subspace sense: if it factors through a closed subspace $Z\hookrightarrow H_0$, closedness and density give $|Z|=|H_0|$. The same factorization lemma, applied to the identity of the reduced space $H_0$, factors that identity through $Z$, making this subobject all of $H_0$. We will construct the diagram for $V_0,H_0$ and then compose with their maps to $V,H$.

source.place: Tag 089G, paragraph after equation-start-with; Tag 03JJ and reduction Tag 03IQ.

proof.text: Choose an affine etale chart $e:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ whose point image contains $a(\mathfrak m_A)$, by choosing a point of an atlas and an affine neighbourhood [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The pullback $T=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_X\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a scheme etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its point image contains the closed point: representatives of $a(\mathfrak m_A)$ and the chosen chart point agree after a common field extension, giving a field point of this pullback [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Since etale scheme maps are flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], apply [lem-a1-flat-valuation-lifting] to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the identity base map. This yields an injective local map $A\hookrightarrow A_1$ and $a_1:\operatorname{Spec}A_1\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ over $X$. Set $K_1=\operatorname{Frac}(A_1)$. The generic equality gives $\eta_1:\operatorname{Spec}K_1\to H_1=H_0\times_X\operatorname{Spec}R$. Put $V_1=V_0\times_X\operatorname{Spec}R$. The projection $H_1\to H_0$ is etale, hence flat by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The scheme-theoretic image of $V_0\to H_0$ is all of $H_0$, by step 1 and the minimality statement of [lem-sfb-stack-schematic-image-qc]. Its flat-base-change clause gives scheme-theoretic image $H_1$ for $V_1\to H_1$. The latter is a quasi-compact open immersion by the original affine-test hypothesis. Write $p_1:H_1\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ for the projection.

source.place: Tag 089G, Reduction to the case Y affine; Tags 089F and 089E.

proof.text: Choose an affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\to H_1$ whose image contains the point represented by $\eta_1$. The atlas and the definition of point equivalence give a field extension $K_1\hookrightarrow K_2$ and a lift $\operatorname{Spec}K_2\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $\eta_1$ after this extension: the two representatives of this point agree over a common field [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Extend $A_1$ to a valuation subring $A_2\subseteq K_2$ with fraction field $K_2$ dominating $A_1$, by [lemma-nagata-valuation-ring-extension]. It inherits $R\to A_1\to A_2$, and its generic map to $H_1$ is the composite through $\operatorname{Spec}B$. This explicitly preserves the original generic diagram and keeps the composite $A\hookrightarrow A_2$ injective and local.

source.place: Tag 089G, first paragraph after reducing Y to Spec(R), enlarging K and its valuation ring.

proof.text: As a $B$-algebra $K_2$ has the explicit surjective presentation $P=B[T_x\mid x\in K_2]\twoheadrightarrow K_2$, $T_x\mapsto x$. Let $z\in\operatorname{Spec}P$ be its kernel point, whose residue field is exactly $K_2$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat]. The etale map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to H_1$ is flat, and their composite $t:\operatorname{Spec}P\to H_1$ is flat, by the flatness, composition and scheme-base-change clauses of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to algebraic spaces as discrete stacks. All maps between algebraic spaces are representable by algebraic spaces: each scheme test gives the sheaf fibre product [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Apply the flat-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-stack-schematic-image-qc] to $V_1\to H_1$ and $t$: the projection $W=V_1\times_{H_1}\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ has scheme-theoretic image all of $\operatorname{Spec}P$. It is a quasi-compact open immersion, being the pullback of $V\hookrightarrow H$ to this affine test, and $W$ is a scheme because open immersions are representable by open immersions of schemes. Thus the scheme valuation-probe result applies.

source.place: Tag 089G, Choose a polynomial algebra P over B and a B-algebra surjection P to K; Tag 089E.

proof.text: Take the chosen scheme valuation probe [def-nagata-dense-valuation-probe, lemma-nagata-dense-valuation-probe] of $W\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ at $z$. Its hypotheses hold: the target is affine, the map is quasi-compact, and its scheme-theoretic image is the whole target by step 4. It gives a valuation ring $D_0$ with fraction field $L$, a map $d:\operatorname{Spec}D_0\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ centred at $z$, and a compatible $\operatorname{Spec}L\to W$. Put $F=D_0/\mathfrak m_{D_0}$. Since the closed point maps to the kernel of $P\twoheadrightarrow K_2$, the composite $P\to D_0\to F$ factors uniquely as $P\twoheadrightarrow K_2\hookrightarrow F$; the second map is injective because it is a unital map of fields. Let $\alpha_0:\operatorname{Spec}D_0\to H_1\to H_0\to H$ be the composite of $d$, and let $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to W\to V$ be the generic map. Then $\alpha_0|_{\operatorname{Spec}L}=hu$. Its closed-fibre map $\operatorname{Spec}F\to H$ is exactly the original $\eta$ after $K\hookrightarrow K_1\hookrightarrow K_2\hookrightarrow F$, since both are induced by the displayed factorization of $P\to F$.

source.place: Tag 089G, application of Tag 089B to the closed point Spec(K) in Spec(P), giving the B-algebra map into the residue field.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-valuation-ring-extension] to $A_2\subseteq K_2$ and $K_2\hookrightarrow F$, obtaining a valuation subring $E\subseteq F$ with fraction field $F$ dominating $A_2$. Define $C=\{x\in D_0:\overline{x}\in E\}$. By [lemma-nagata-composite-valuation-ring], $C$ is a valuation ring with fraction field $L$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_{D_0}\subseteq C$, and the residue restriction gives $C/\mathfrak q\cong E$. In particular $\mathfrak q$ is prime. Use this canonical isomorphism to regard $E$ as $C/\mathfrak q$. The composite $A\hookrightarrow A_1\hookrightarrow A_2\hookrightarrow E$ is injective and local, since contracting the maximal ideal successively gives the maximal ideals of $A_2,A_1,A$.

source.place: Tag 089G, choose the residue-field valuation A double-prime and define C; algebra.tex Tag 088Z.

proof.text: The inclusion $C\subseteq D_0$ identifies $C_{\mathfrak q}$ with $D_0$ by the following fraction calculation. Every $t\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ has nonzero residue in $F$, hence is a unit in $D_0$. Conversely, given $x\in D_0$, write its residue as $a/s$ with $a,s\in E$ and $s\ne0$, using $\operatorname{Frac}(E)=F$. Choose a residue lift $t\in D_0$ of $s$. Then $t\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ and $tx\in C$, since their residues are $s$ and $a$. Thus $x=(tx)/t\in C_{\mathfrak q}$. The maps are injective inside $L$, so this is an equality there. Set $D=C_{\mathfrak q}=D_0$ and transport $\alpha_0$ to $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}D\to H$. Its residue field is $F=\operatorname{Frac}(E)$ and its fraction field is $L$, as required.

source.place: Tag 089G, the statement that A prime is the localization of C at its maximal ideal (immediately after the construction of C); explicit denominator argument supplied.

proof.text: The $R$-algebra structure $R\to P\to D_0$ has residue $R\to K_2\to F$. On $R$ this equals $R\to A_1\to A_2\to E\hookrightarrow F$, by the preserved generic diagram of steps 2 and 3. Hence $R\to D_0$ lands in $C$, defining $b:\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$. Restriction along $C\to D$ gives $p\alpha=bj_D$, since both maps to $X$ factor through the original map $\operatorname{Spec}D_0\to\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Reduction along $C\twoheadrightarrow E$ gives $bi_E=a\operatorname{Spec}(A\hookrightarrow E)$, because on $R$ the residue restriction is exactly $R\to A_1\to E$. Finally step 5 gives $\alpha s_F=\eta\operatorname{Spec}(K\hookrightarrow F)$ and $\alpha|_{\operatorname{Spec}L}=hu$. These four equalities are equalities of the displayed morphisms, not merely of their underlying points.
